// Generated by logos-lidl-gen --provider from the `names` LIDL contract — do not edit.
//
// The common module-impl C ABI (logos_module_impl.h) around a Rust impl:
// implement `NamesModule` on your type and define the install hook:
//
//     #[no_mangle]
//     pub extern "Rust" fn logos_module_install() { install::<YourImpl>(); }
//
// The first dispatch invokes it lazily — a plain symbol reference, so
// no ctor/init-section tricks are needed for static linking.

use std::ffi::{c_char, c_int, c_void, CStr, CString};
use std::sync::Mutex;

/// This module's own name, from the LIDL contract.
///
/// The ORIGIN of every outbound call this image makes: it is what
/// capability_module checks against its known-caller roster and the
/// target's access policy, what the target files the minted token
/// under, and what a callee's `current_caller()` reports.
pub const LOGOS_MODULE_NAME: &str = "names";

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct RustModuleContext {
    pub module_path: String,
    pub instance_id: String,
    pub instance_persistence_path: String,
}

static CONTEXT: Mutex<Option<RustModuleContext>> = Mutex::new(None);

/// The module identity/context stamped by the host (None before
/// set_context — mirrors LogosModuleContext::isContextReady()).
pub fn context() -> Option<RustModuleContext> {
    CONTEXT.lock().unwrap().clone()
}

type EmitCb = extern "C" fn(*const c_char, *const c_char, *mut c_void);
struct EmitState {
    cb: Option<(EmitCb, usize)>,
}
unsafe impl Send for EmitState {}
static EMIT: Mutex<EmitState> = Mutex::new(EmitState { cb: None });

fn emit_event(name: &str, payload: &serde_json::Value) {
    let state = EMIT.lock().unwrap();
    if let Some((cb, ud)) = state.cb {
        let name_c = CString::new(name).unwrap_or_default();
        let json_c = CString::new(payload.to_string()).unwrap_or_default();
        cb(name_c.as_ptr(), json_c.as_ptr(), ud as *mut c_void);
    }
}

// Contract trait `NamesModule` is author-declared in this crate (Rust-first
// flow); the scaffold generates everything around it.

type DispatchFn = fn(&str, &[serde_json::Value]) -> Option<serde_json::Value>;
type EnsureFn = fn(bool);
// Reaches the author's impl from the teardown C export, which is a
// free function with no `T` -- exactly why `dispatch` is reached
// this way too.
type AboutToUnloadFn = fn() -> i32;
struct Registered {
    dispatch: DispatchFn,
    ensure: EnsureFn,
    // Read only by the teardown export, which is emitted for
    // protocol >= 0.5; an older module registers the hook and
    // never calls it.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    about_to_unload: AboutToUnloadFn,
}
static REGISTERED: Mutex<Option<Registered>> = Mutex::new(None);
// A concurrency:"single" module runs entirely on one thread (its
// subprocess event loop): install / on_context_ready / dispatch all touch
// INSTANCE from that thread, so the impl never crosses threads and need
// not be Send. This single-threaded Sync wrapper lets a non-Send impl
// live in a static (cf. the EmitState unsafe impl above).
struct SingleInstance(Mutex<Option<Box<dyn std::any::Any>>>);
unsafe impl Sync for SingleInstance {}
static INSTANCE: SingleInstance = SingleInstance(Mutex::new(None));
static HOOK_FIRED: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool = std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false);

/// Install `T` as the module implementation (Default-constructed once).
///
/// `on_context_ready` fires AT MODULE LOAD — as soon as the host has
/// delivered both the context (set_context) and the event plumbing
/// (set_emit_callback), which the glue does during registration,
/// before the module is published for inbound calls. This matches
/// C++'s onContextReady-in-onInit semantics: subscriptions, outbound
/// calls and typed emission all work from the hook without waiting
/// for a first inbound dispatch. (For hosts that never wire an emit
/// callback, the hook still fires before the first dispatch.)
pub fn install<T: NamesModule + Default>() {
    fn ensure_impl<T: NamesModule + Default>(require_emit: bool) {
        let mut guard = INSTANCE.0.lock().unwrap();
        if guard.is_none() {
            *guard = Some(Box::new(T::default()));
        }
        if HOOK_FIRED.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst) {
            return;
        }
        let Some(ctx) = context() else { return; };
        if require_emit && EMIT.lock().unwrap().cb.is_none() {
            return;
        }
        if let Some(imp) = guard.as_mut().unwrap().downcast_mut::<T>() {
            HOOK_FIRED.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
            imp.on_context_ready(&ctx);
        }
    }

        // stable Rust cannot detect an optional method, so the

        0

            "lidl" => {
                                     if !args.is_empty() { return Some(logos_rust_sdk::args::invalid_args("names", 0, args.len())); }
                                     let result = "module names {\n  version \"0.17.0\"\n  depends []\n\n  method recipient(name: tstr) -> tstr description \"Where to send a payment for `name` (`jef.lez` or `jef`). The value is\\n`{name, display, public, public_hex, private}`: `private` is\\n`{nullifier_public_key, viewing_public_key}` in hex or null, and\\n`public` is an account ID or null. Prefer `private` when it is there.\\nA name that forwards (its `forward` entry, SPEC.md §7) is paid where it\\npoints, one hop: then `name` is the target and `forwarded_from` the name\\nasked for, which a payer must be shown. A null value means the name is\\nnot registered.\"\n  method resolve(name: tstr) -> tstr description \"Everything `name` resolves to: `{name, display, owner_tag, expires,\\nnever, lapsed, deposit, account, npk, vpk, texts}`. A name held by a\\ndeposit never expires: `expires` is null, `never` true and `lapsed`\\nfalse; `deposit` is what its deposit account holds (decimal text), which\\na release refunds. In fee mode `expires` is in milliseconds and `lapsed`\\nis true once it has passed. `owner_tag` is the holder's tag (hex): the\\nchain never names the holder. A null value means it is not registered,\\nwhich includes a fee-mode name that lapsed more than 30 days ago.\\n`forward` is the name it points to (SPEC.md §7, Forwarding), or null:\\n`resolve` doesn't follow it, so the name's holder can still edit it.\"\n  method page(name: tstr) -> tstr description \"The page published under `name`: `{content_type, bytes, text}`, where\\n`text` is the body if it is valid UTF-8. A null value means no page.\\nThe page is written by the name's owner: treat it as untrusted content.\"\n  method page_view(name: tstr) -> tstr description \"The page published under `name`, made safe to show inside an app:\\n`{content_type, bytes, kind, title, html, text, truncated}`. `kind` is\\n`html`, `text` or `file`. For an HTML page, `html` is the body rewritten\\nto an allowlist Qt's rich text can draw (headings, paragraphs, lists,\\ntables, emphasis, code, and links to `http:`/`https:` URLs only; no\\nscripts, styles, images, attributes or comments), and `title` is its\\n`<title>` as plain text; both are null otherwise. `text` is the page's\\nown source, as in `page`, to be shown only as plain text. At most 64 KB\\nof a page is read; `truncated` says it was cut. A null value means no page.\"\n  method page_preview(body: tstr) -> tstr description \"`body`, a page not yet published, as `page_view` would show it: an\\nHTML body (one that opens with a tag) sanitized the same way, anything\\nelse as plain text. For previewing a page while it is written.\"\n  method avatar(name: tstr) -> tstr description \"The picture in `name`'s `avatar` entry, decoded, for an app that can't\\nload a `data:` URL: `{width, height, pixels}`, where `pixels` is base64\\nof RGBA8 bytes, row by row from the top left. At most 128 pixels a side\\n(a larger picture is scaled down, nearest neighbour). Only PNG is\\ndecoded. A null value means the name has no avatar this can decode.\"\n  method reverse(account: tstr) -> tstr description \"The name `account` (base58) has published for itself, or null. The\\nanswer is checked against the name's own record, so it cannot be spoofed.\"\n  method normalize(input: tstr) -> tstr description \"The bare name for what a person typed (`Jef.LEZ` gives `jef`), or an\\nempty string if it is not a valid name. Makes no network call.\"\n  method wallet() -> tstr description \"The open LEZ wallet: `{accounts: [{account, balance, funded, name}],\\nprivate_accounts: [account]}`. `accounts` are its public accounts,\\nfunded ones first; `balance` is decimal text and `name` is the name the\\naccount has published, or null. Fails if the LEZ wallet is not\\ninstalled or not open.\"\n  method mine() -> tstr description \"The names this device remembers that the open wallet holds, and the\\nregistrations it has under way: `{names: [{name, display, owner,\\nexpires, never, lapsed}], pending: [{name, display, owner, stage,\\nready_at, tx}]}`. `owner` is the wallet's account that holds the name.\\nA pending `stage` is `committed` (call `register_name` again from\\n`ready_at`, in milliseconds) or `revealed` (sent; it shows in `names`\\nonce it lands). The chain keeps no list of names, so this is the\\ndevice's own memory: every name registered from here, and every name\\npassed to `keep`.\"\n  method keep(name: tstr) -> tstr description \"Remembers `name` on this device, if the open wallet holds it, so `mine`\\nkeeps returning it. Fails for a name the wallet does not hold. The value is the bare name.\"\n  method deposit(name: tstr) -> tstr description \"What registering `name` takes: `{name, display, tier, deposit, mode,\\nclaims_until}`.\\n`tier` is `normal`, `three` (a three-character name, at the higher\\ndeposit) or `locked` (one or two characters: only the registry's admin\\nmay register it, and `deposit` is null). `deposit` is decimal text in\\nthe native token's base units, held while the name is and refunded on\\nrelease. `mode` is `deposit`, `fee` or `unconfigured`; in fee mode\\n`deposit` is 0 and `fee` gives the price of a one-year term instead.\\n`claims_until` is null, or while names from the earlier chain can still be\\nclaimed, when that ends, in milliseconds of chain time: until then a holder's\\nclaim replaces a registration of their name, and whoever registered it loses\\nthe deposit to them. An app must say so first (SPEC.md section 8.4).\\nMakes one network read, besides deriving the name.\"\n  method settings() -> tstr description \"The registry's settings: `{mode, deposits: {normal, three}, admin,\\ntreasury, prices: {30d, 1y, 5y}, claims_until}`, amounts as decimal text,\\n`claims_until` as in `deposit`. A null value\\nmeans the registry has no settings yet (it charges nothing, and locks\\none- and two-character names).\"\n  method register_name(name: tstr, owner: tstr, private_account: tstr) -> tstr description \"Registers `name` to `owner` (base58), a public account in the open\\nwallet, which pays the deposit (see `deposit`). Registering is two\\nsteps, so that nobody watching pending transactions can take the name\\nfirst: the first call sends a commitment, which hides the name, and\\nanswers `stage: \\\"committed\\\"` with `ready_at` (milliseconds, chain time,\\nabout 15 minutes on). Calling `register_name` again from then on sends the\\nreveal that claims the name (`stage: \\\"revealed\\\"`), and once that has\\nlanded, answers `stage: \\\"registered\\\"` without sending anything. A call\\nbefore `ready_at` sends nothing. The commitment is kept on this device\\nand stays usable for 24 hours. The value also has `deposit` (or `fee`)\\nand `tier`; `tx` is null when nothing was sent.\\n`private_account` makes the name payable privately from the start: one\\nof the wallet's private accounts (base58), `auto` for a new private\\naccount made for this name alone, or empty to set nothing. It is used by\\nthe reveal; given at commit time it is remembered for it, and the account\\n`auto` makes is remembered too, so a retried reveal reuses it.\"\n  method receive_privately(name: tstr, private_account: tstr) -> tstr description \"Makes `name` payable privately and only privately: publishes the\\nreceiving keys of `private_account` (as for `register_name`; `auto` makes a\\nnew private account each time) and removes any public account from the name.\"\n  method set_account(name: tstr, account: tstr) -> tstr description \"Points `name` at a public account (base58). The card keys are\\n`display`, `bio`, `avatar` (a `data:image/...` URL), `theme` (`light`,\\n`dark` or `auto`), `color` (`#rrggbb`), `font` (`sans`, `serif`, `mono`\\nor `rounded`) and `cid` (a Logos Storage content ID); any other key of\\n1-32 characters of a-z, 0-9, `-`, `_` or `.` works too. Returns false and changes nothing if it is not an\\naccount ID, or is the native token.\"\n  method cli_token_holdings(account: tstr) -> tstr description \"What the names CLI's accounts hold of each token, public and private:\\n`{token_program, holdings: [{account, account_kind, definition, name,\\nbalance}], updating, error}`, only `account`'s (written `Public/<id>`\\nor `Private/<id>`) unless it is empty. `name` is the definition's own\\nname (the token maker's text, cleaned) or null; amounts are decimal\\ntext in base units. Read in the background (a private account's\\nholdings need the wallet to catch up with the chain, up to a minute or\\ntwo): the answer comes at once with the last read, null until the\\nfirst ends, and `updating` while a newer one is on the way.\"\n  method cli_token_pending() -> tstr description \"The token credits sent to the wallet's private keys and not yet\\nreceived: `{token_program, pending: [{position, definition, name,\\namount, to}], updating, error}`, `to` the private account they credit.\\nFrom the same read as `cli_token_holdings`. `cli_token_receive` takes them.\"\n  method cli_token_info(definition: tstr) -> tstr description \"What the token `definition` (its definition's account ID) is:\\n`{definition, name, supply, authority}`; `authority` may mint more,\\nnull for a fixed supply. Read from the chain through the CLI (seconds),\\nthen kept for 30 seconds.\"\n  method watched_tokens() -> tstr description \"The tokens added to the wallet by address, for the token program in\\nuse: `[{definition, name}]`, in the order added; `name` is the\\ndefinition's own (as `cli_token_info` read it when added) or null.\"\n  method watch_token(definition: tstr, watch: bool) -> tstr description \"Adds (`watch`) or removes the token `definition` (its definition's\\naccount ID) from the wallet's list, so it shows before any of it is\\nheld. Adding reads the definition through the CLI first, so an ID that\\nisn't a token of the program in use is refused. Gives the list as\\n`watched_tokens` does. Kept on this device, per token program.\"\n  method cli_token_send(definition: tstr, amount: tstr, to: tstr, from_private: bool, to_public: bool) -> tstr description \"Sends `amount` (base units, decimal text up to 2^128 - 1) of the token\\n`definition` (its definition's account ID) to `to`: a name, a public\\naccount written `Public/<id>`, or one of the wallet's own\\n`Private/<id>`. From the wallet's main private account with\\n`from_private`, else its main public one. To a name it goes to the\\nname's private receiving keys, where it waits until its holder receives\\nit, unless `to_public` (or the name has only a public account). A\\nwallet job (`names token send`): one block from the public account to\\na public account; otherwise proven on this computer, 7-12 minutes.\\nOnce it ends, its `job` state has `tx`, `block` and, if it failed,\\n`problem`. Everything is checked before the CLI runs.\"\n  method cli_token_receive() -> tstr description \"Receives every token credit waiting for the wallet's private keys\\n(`names token receive`), as a wallet job: one proven transaction per\\ncredit, 7-12 minutes each, paid from a private account's LEZ. A job\\nstops after 45 minutes; credits it didn't reach stay pending and the\\nnext receive takes them. Its ended `job` state has `applied` (how many\\nwere received), `nothing` (there was nothing to receive) and `problem`.\"\n  method cli_accounts() -> tstr description \"Every account of the names CLI's wallet: `[{account, kind, label,\\nbalance, default, public_key, npk}]`. `account` is written `Public/<id>` or\\n`Private/<id>`; `label` the nickname given here, or null; `balance`\\ndecimal text (a public account's read from the chain, a private one's as\\nthe wallet last saw it), or null if it couldn't be read; `default` marks\\nthe account of its kind the wallet pays and registers from. `public_key`\\n(hex, public accounts only) is what someone needs to pay a public\\naccount the chain hasn't seen yet; `npk` (hex, private accounts only)\\nis the key a name's profile publishes to be paid there, so it tells\\nwhich name an account receives for. The wallet catches up with the chain\\nfirst: seconds to a minute or two, so ask with a long timeout.\"\n  method cli_account_new(kind: tstr, label: tstr) -> tstr description \"Makes a new `kind` (`public` or `private`) account in the wallet, with\\nthe nickname `label` (empty for none, at most 40 characters), and gives\\nit as a `cli_accounts` entry. Nothing is sent and nothing is paid. A\\nwallet without a default account of that kind makes it the default.\\nRefused while a CLI job runs, since a job saves the wallet when it ends.\"\n  method cli_account_label(account: tstr, label: tstr) -> tstr description \"Gives the wallet's `account` (`Public/<id>` or `Private/<id>`) the\\nnickname `label`; an empty one clears it. `{account, label}`.\"\n  method cli_account_use(account: tstr) -> tstr description \"Pays and registers from `account` (`Public/<id>` or `Private/<id>`)\\nfrom now on: it becomes the default of its kind, and `cli_balance`,\\n`cli_pay`, `cli_register` and the rest use it. A\\nhidden account (`chain_account_remove`) is left out while the node shows\\nit holding nothing.\"\n  method chain_stake() -> tstr description \"Stake: `{staked, notes, keys, epoch, next_epoch_in_s, claimable,\\nvouchers, reward_per_voucher}`, amounts as decimal text. `staked` is\\nwhat the node's notes put in the leader lottery (any note on its keys,\\nonce in an epoch's snapshot); `next_epoch_in_s` is null when the node\\ndoesn't say. A hash not sent from here fails, saying why.\"\n  method chain_claim(send: bool) -> tstr description \"The node's leader rewards: without `send`, `{claimable, vouchers,\\nreward_per_voucher}`. With `send`, one transaction claims ONE voucher\\n(the node's `leader_claim` makes a single claim op) and pays its own\\nfee from the node's leader funding key, which can be more than the\\nreward: `{hash, claimed, fee, vouchers_left, claimable_left}`, with\\n`warning` when the fee was more than `claimed`. Fails when there is\\nnothing to claim.\"\n  method chain_split(from_key: tstr, amount: tstr, send: bool) -> tstr description \"Splits `amount` off the node key `from_key` into a note of its own, so a\\nbridge can deposit exactly that much: a send from the key to itself (its\\nchange comes back as another note). The notes it spends\\nleave the stake, and the new ones join it within two epochs.\"\n  method chain_bridge(from_key: tstr, to: tstr, amount: tstr, send: bool) -> tstr description \"Bridges exactly `amount` from the node key `from_key` into the LEZ public\\naccount `to` (`Public/<id>`; empty is the names wallet's default public\\none): one note of exactly that value is deposited on LEZ's channel through\\nBasecamp's node (`channel_deposit_with_notes`), its fee paid from the key's\\nother notes, at most `fee`. Without `send` the plan `{sent: false, hash:\\nnull, to, amount, total, notes, fee, note, needs_split, channel, lines}`;\\n`needs_split` is true (and `note` null) when no note holds exactly\\n`amount`: `chain_split` first. LEZ credits it\\nonce the block holding it is final.\"\n  method chain_account_new(label: tstr) -> tstr description \"Makes a new account on the node: a key in its keystore, labelled\\n`label` (at most 40 characters; empty for none): `{key, title, label,\\nready, note}`. Its secret stays in the node's keystore.\"\n  method chain_account_label(key: tstr, label: tstr) -> tstr description \"Labels the node key `key` (empty takes the label off): `{key, label}`.\\nLabels are kept by this module, and shown by `chain_accounts`.\"\n  method chain_account_remove(key: tstr) -> tstr description \"Hides an account made with `chain_account_new` once the node uses it\\nand it holds nothing: `{key, title, hidden, note}`. Asks nobody.\"\n  method account_balances() -> tstr description \"The LEZ balance of each account this app has been given, `[{account,\\naccount_kind, balance, updating, error}]`; `balance` is decimal text\\nor null until first read. Balances are read in the background and the\\nanswer comes at once with the last one read (`updating` while a newer\\none is on the way); ask again for a fresh one. A private account's\\nbalance is only here if the person gave this app that account.\"\n  method propose_transfer(asset: tstr, amount: tstr, destination: tstr) -> tstr description \"Asks to send `amount` (base units, decimal digits) of `asset` to\\n`destination`: a name, or a public account written `Public/<id>`.\\n`asset` is `LEZ`, the native token (empty also means LEZ), or a token\\nof the wallet's token program, written as its definition's account ID\\n(base58); the prompt then shows the token's name and what the Program\\nRegistry says about the token program. Only the app that made a request can read it.\"\n  method cancel_request(request_id: tstr) -> tstr description \"Withdraws this app's own request while it is still pending.\"\n  method drop_access() -> tstr description \"Gives up the access this app was given. `{revoked}`.\"\n  method pending_requests() -> tstr description \"The requests waiting for the person, oldest first, each with\\neverything its prompt shows and `choices`, the accounts it may use:\\n`[{account, account_kind, pays, label, granted}]`, all in the names\\nCLI's wallet: a payment comes from its main public or private account\\n(`pays`), a call is signed by any of its public accounts (those beyond\\nthe main one are listed from a read in the background, so they may\\nappear a moment later). Names app only.\"\n  method approve_request(request_id: tstr, account: tstr) -> tstr description \"Approves request `request_id` with `account`, one of its `choices`\\n(for access, one or more separated by commas). If the wallet\\nis busy the request stays pending and the error says so. Names app only.\"\n  method reject_request(request_id: tstr) -> tstr description \"Rejects request `request_id`. Names app only.\"\n  method app_grants() -> tstr description \"Which apps have access to which accounts: `[{app, accounts, since}]`.\\nNames app only.\"\n  method revoke_app(app: tstr) -> tstr description \"Takes back all access `app` was given. Names app only.\"\n  method app_secret(account: tstr, scope: tstr, context_hex: tstr, tag: tstr, first: int, count: int) -> tstr description \"Values derived for the calling app from `account` (one of the accounts it was given):\\n`SHA256(tag | m_i)` for `i` in `first..first + count` (1 to 64), where `m_i` is a\\nmaster value the wallet makes from the account's own key, the app's name as Basecamp\\ngives it, `scope` (1-64 printable ASCII) and `context_hex` (up to 256 bytes) and never\\ngives out. The same call gives the same values after the wallet is restored from its\\nrecovery phrase. The first call for an (app, account, scope) asks the person: the value\\nis then `{granted: false, request}`; once they approve, `{granted: true, account, scope,\\ntag, first, values: [hex]}`. `tag` is 1-32 printable ASCII.\"\n  method propose_private_call(account: tstr, call_json: tstr, summary: tstr) -> tstr description \"Asks the wallet to build, prove and send a privacy-preserving transaction from the\\nprivate `account` (one this app was given) across up to 4 programs. `call_json` is\\n`{programs, accounts, message, openings, fee_payer, declared, reveal_account}`\\n(PROVIDER-SDK.md). The wallet simulates it against the chain first and shows the person\\nwhat it really changes; `request_status` gives `check` (`running`, `ready` or\\n`failed`; a call the wallet refuses is `ready` with `sheet.refused` true and can't be\\napproved) and, once approved, `phase`. `summary` (280 characters) is shown as the app's words.\"\n  method declare_programs(programs_json: tstr, reason: tstr) -> tstr description \"Declares the programs this app will ask the wallet to sign calls to someone else pays\\nfor (`propose_relayed_call`): a JSON array of 1 to 8 program IDs. The person approves\\nit once (`reason`, 280 characters, is shown as the app's words); a relayed call naming\\nany other program is refused. A request, as for access.\"\n  method propose_relayed_call(account: tstr, call_json: tstr, summary: tstr) -> tstr description \"Asks the wallet to sign, as the public `account` (one this app was given; a never-used\\none too), a call whose fee ANOTHER account pays: `call_json` is `{program, message,\\naccounts, fee: {payer, gas_limit, tip, max_fee}, privacy}` (PROVIDER-SDK.md, \\\"Calls\\nsomeone else pays for\\\"). The wallet builds the transaction itself and shows the person\\nwhat it built; once approved, `request_status` gives `transaction` (the half-signed\\ntransaction, hex borsh) and `hash`. The wallet sends nothing and pays nothing. LEZ 0.4\\nonly for now.\"\n  method resign_relayed_call(request_id: tstr) -> tstr description \"Signs this app's approved relayed call `request_id` again, without asking the person,\\nwhen the fee payer's nonce has moved (a relay that had another transaction in flight)\\nand NOTHING else has: the same account and account nonce, program, bytes, actors, payer,\\ngas limit, tip and max fee. At most 3 times, within 10 minutes of the approval. Any other\\nchange is refused: propose the call again for the person to approve. The value is the\\nrequest, with the new `transaction` and `hash`.\"\n  method propose_token_source(token_program: tstr, definitions_json: tstr) -> tstr description \"Asks the person to list a token program's definitions in their holdings, with the\\nnames, symbols and decimals given: `definitions_json` is `[{definition, name, symbol,\\ndecimals, origin}]` (up to 16).\"\n  method token_sources() -> tstr description \"The token sources the person accepted: `[{token_program, definitions, app, since}]`.\"\n  method secret_grants() -> tstr description \"The secret grants: `[{app, account, scope, since}]`. Names app only.\"\n  method revoke_secret(app: tstr, account: tstr, scope: tstr) -> tstr description \"Takes back one secret grant. `{revoked}`. Names app only.\"\n  method private_call_control(request_id: tstr, action: tstr) -> tstr description \"Pauses, resumes or cancels an approved private call while it is still being planned\\nor proven: `action` is `pause`, `resume` or `cancel`. Refused once it is being sent.\\nNames app only.\"\n  method token_source_holdings() -> tstr description \"What the wallet's accounts hold of every token source's definitions: `[{token_program,\\nholdings: [{account, account_kind, definition, name, symbol, decimals, origin,\\nbalance}], updating, error}]`. Read in the background. Names app only.\"\n  method cli_token_send_source(token_program: tstr, definition: tstr, amount: tstr, to: tstr, from_private: bool, to_public: bool) -> tstr description \"Sends a token of a registered token source, as `cli_token_send` does for the wallet's\\nown token program. Names app only.\"\n  method remove_token_source(token_program: tstr) -> tstr description \"Forgets a token source. `{removed}`. Names app only.\"\n  method chain_inscribe(from_key: tstr, text: tstr, send: bool) -> tstr description \"Inscribes a testimonial (`{\\\"submission\\\": \\\"lp-0022:names-wallet\\\", \\\"text\\\"}`, text\\n1-1024 bytes) on the Logos Blockchain from the node key `from_key`, which pays the\\nfee. Each key has its own Ed25519 inscription key, made here once and kept 0600,\\nand its own channel (`sha256(\\\"lp-0022:testimonial:\\\" || signer)`), which the first\\ninscription creates and later ones extend. Without `send` the plan `{from, balance,\\nsigner, channel, parent, first, submission, text, bytes, msg_id, fee_estimate}`\\n(the fee the node asks now, or absent when it couldn't say). A plan moves and\\nholds nothing: the node prices it on stand-ins for the key's notes (`chain_fee`),\\nso any number of plans, sends and splits can follow at once. Through logosctl, write\\na text or key that is only digits, or `true`/`false`, as `str:2026`:\\nlogosctl 0.3.2 sends it as a number or boolean otherwise, and the host refuses the\\ncall (\\\"dispatch_failed: expected string\\\") before names runs.\"\n  method propose_inscription(text: tstr) -> tstr description \"Any app: asks for `text` (a testimonial, 1-1024 bytes) to be inscribed on the\\nLogos Blockchain. The person picks which of the node's chain accounts inscribes\\nit and pays its fee, and approves it in the Names app. No LEZ access is needed\\nfirst: the request names no account. When the node can't list them (stopped, say), each request\\nis still listed, with `choices` empty and `node` saying why, so it can be rejected.\\nA choice carries the `label` the person gave the account (or its keystore `title`),\\nand an account hidden while it holds nothing is left out, as in `chain_accounts`.\\nThe fee for a choice is `chain_inscribe(key, text, false)`'s `fee_estimate`, which\\nholds nothing. `pending_requests` doesn't list these. Names app only.\"\n  method approve_inscription(request_id: tstr, from_key: tstr) -> tstr description \"Approves inscription request `request_id` with the node key `from_key`: it is\\ninscribed (`chain_inscribe`) and the request is `done` with `tx`. Refused before\\nanything is sent (a key the node doesn't hold, too little for the fee), the\\nrequest stays pending. Names app only.\"\n}\n".to_string();
                                     Some(serde_json::Value::from(result))
                                 }
            _ => None,
        }
    }
    *REGISTERED.lock().unwrap() = Some(Registered {
        dispatch: dispatch_impl::<T>,
        ensure: ensure_impl::<T>,
        about_to_unload: about_to_unload_impl::<T>,
    });
}

/// Run the author's install hook (once) and give the ready-latch a
/// chance to fire `on_context_ready`. Called from every C-ABI entry
/// point: set_context / set_emit_callback latch on full wiring;
/// dispatch passes require_emit = false as the no-event-host fallback.
fn ensure_ready(require_emit: bool) {
    // FIRST, and before the author's install hook can construct
    // anything: tell the SDK the name this image announces when it
    // calls out. Every generated path that reaches author code runs
    // through here -- install/T::default, on_context_ready, dispatch,
    // and (transitively) about_to_unload, which answers 0 unless
    // install already ran -- so the origin is set before the first
    // outbound client exists. Without a name the SDK announces
    // nothing and the capability handshake fails closed; with the
    // wrong one ("core") it authorized as the host. The SDK also
    // keys its client cache by origin, so even a client built before
    // this ran cannot be reused after it. Idempotent: a OnceLock set.
    logos_rust_sdk::set_module_origin(LOGOS_MODULE_NAME);
    if REGISTERED.lock().unwrap().is_none() {
        unsafe { __logos_install_hook::logos_module_install() };
    }
    let ensure = REGISTERED.lock().unwrap().as_ref().map(|r| r.ensure);
    if let Some(f) = ensure {
        f(require_emit);
    }
}

mod __logos_install_hook {
    // Defined by the module author (a #[no_mangle] fn at crate root):
    // call `install::<YourImpl>()` once. Scoped inside a module so the
    // declaration and the author's definition don't collide by path;
    // they meet at the symbol level. Referenced (not just expected) so
    // static linking always pulls the author's object in — invoked
    // lazily on first dispatch.
    extern "Rust" {
        pub(super) fn logos_module_install();
    }
}

fn to_c_string(s: String) -> *mut c_char {
    CString::new(s).map(CString::into_raw).unwrap_or(std::ptr::null_mut())
}

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn logos_module_dispatch(method: *const c_char, args_json: *const c_char) -> *mut c_char {
    if method.is_null() { return std::ptr::null_mut(); }
    let method = unsafe { CStr::from_ptr(method) }.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
    let args: Vec<serde_json::Value> = if args_json.is_null() {
        Vec::new()
    } else {
        let raw = unsafe { CStr::from_ptr(args_json) }.to_string_lossy();
        match serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&raw) {
            Ok(serde_json::Value::Array(a)) => a,
            _ => return std::ptr::null_mut(),
        }
    };
    ensure_ready(false);
    // Copy the dispatch fn pointer out and RELEASE the REGISTERED
    // lock BEFORE running the handler. A concurrency:"multi" module's
    // glue calls this from worker threads; holding the mutex across
    // the handler would serialize every call (peak overlap 1).
    // dispatch_impl resolves the instance internally (a cloned Arc in
    // multi mode, the boxed instance behind the SingleInstance mutex in
    // single mode) without holding REGISTERED, so dropping the lock here
    // first is safe. Same release-before-call shape as ensure_ready.
    let dispatch = match REGISTERED.lock().unwrap().as_ref() { Some(r) => r.dispatch, None => return std::ptr::null_mut() };
    match dispatch(&method, &args) {
        Some(value) => to_c_string(value.to_string()),
        None => std::ptr::null_mut(),
    }
}

    to_c_string("[{\"description\":\"Where to send a payment for `name` (`jef.lez` or `jef`). }

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn logos_module_set_context(
    module_path: *const c_char,
    instance_id: *const c_char,
    instance_persistence_path: *const c_char,
) {
    fn s(p: *const c_char) -> String {
        if p.is_null() { String::new() } else { unsafe { CStr::from_ptr(p) }.to_string_lossy().into_owned() }
    }
    *CONTEXT.lock().unwrap() = Some(RustModuleContext {
        module_path: s(module_path),
        instance_id: s(instance_id),
        instance_persistence_path: s(instance_persistence_path),
    });
    ensure_ready(true);
}

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn logos_module_set_emit_callback(cb: Option<EmitCb>, user_data: *mut c_void) {
    EMIT.lock().unwrap().cb = cb.map(|f| (f, user_data as usize));
    ensure_ready(true);
}

static TOKENS: Mutex<Vec<(String, String)>> = Mutex::new(Vec::new());

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn logos_module_accept_token(module_name: *const c_char, token: *const c_char) -> c_int {
    if module_name.is_null() || token.is_null() { return -1; }
    let name = unsafe { CStr::from_ptr(module_name) }.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
    let tok = unsafe { CStr::from_ptr(token) }.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
    // THE OUTBOUND DOOR. Hand the host-issued token to the SDK's
    // protocol stack so this module's *outbound* calls authenticate —
    // the same stack the typed client wrappers invoke through.
    //
    // ONE MEANING ONLY, as of protocol 0.8: the module's OWN anchor,
    // seeded by the Qt glue's onInit. A CALLER's token goes through
    // logos_module_accept_inbound_token instead. Do not merge them —
    // one value written through the wrong door made every capability
    // grant silently bidirectional.
    logos_rust_sdk::save_token(&name, &tok);
    TOKENS.lock().unwrap().push((name, tok));
    0
}

/// The logos-protocol semver this module was built against
/// (stamped at generation time by the build; never minted here).
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn logos_module_get_protocol_version() -> *const c_char {
    static VERSION: &str = "0.9.0\0";
    VERSION.as_ptr() as *const c_char
}

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn logos_module_string_free(s: *mut c_char) {
    if !s.is_null() {
        unsafe { drop(CString::from_raw(s)) };
    }
}

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn logos_module_grant_host_services(services_json: *const c_char) -> c_int {
    if services_json.is_null() { return -1; }
    unsafe { logos_rust_sdk::grant_host_services(services_json) }
}

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn logos_module_set_unload_done_callback(
    cb: Option<logos_rust_sdk::UnloadDoneCb>,
    user_data: *mut std::os::raw::c_void,
) {
    logos_rust_sdk::set_unload_done_callback(cb, user_data);
}

/// Ask the impl whether it is ready to be unloaded: 0 = Synchronous
/// (proceed), 1 = Asynchronous (wait for unload_finished()).
///
/// A module that was never installed answers 0: there is no instance, so
/// there is nothing to tear down and nothing for the host to wait on.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn logos_module_about_to_unload() -> c_int {
    if let Some(f) = *UNLOAD_HOOK.lock().unwrap() {
        return f();
    }
    let hook = REGISTERED.lock().unwrap().as_ref().map(|r| r.about_to_unload);
    match hook {
        Some(f) => f(),
        None => 0,
    }
}

// Set by logos_install! to a hook resolved at the author's concrete type.
#[allow(dead_code)]
static UNLOAD_HOOK: Mutex<Option<AboutToUnloadFn>> = Mutex::new(None);

#[allow(dead_code)]
fn set_unload_hook(f: AboutToUnloadFn) {
    *UNLOAD_HOOK.lock().unwrap() = Some(f);
}

/// Install `$t` as the module implementation and wire its teardown hook.
///
/// Drop-in for `install::<$t>()`. Implement `logos_rust_sdk::AboutToUnload` for
/// `$t` to be asked before the host unloads this module; without that impl this
/// is exactly `install`.
#[allow(unused_macros)]
macro_rules! logos_install {
    ($t:ty) => {{
        fn __logos_about_to_unload() -> i32 {
            // Exactly one of these two is used, and which one is the whole
            // question being asked -- so the loser is always unused.
            #[allow(unused_imports)]
            use logos_rust_sdk::{UnloadProbe, UnloadProbeDefault, UnloadProbeHooked};
            let guard = INSTANCE.0.lock().unwrap();
            let Some(any) = guard.as_ref() else { return 0 };
            let Some(imp) = any.downcast_ref::<$t>() else { return 0 };
            match (&UnloadProbe::<$t>::new()).probe(&*imp) {
                logos_rust_sdk::Shutdown::Asynchronous => 1,
                logos_rust_sdk::Shutdown::Synchronous => 0,
            }
        }
        set_unload_hook(__logos_about_to_unload);
        install::<$t>();
    }};
}

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn logos_module_set_call_caller(caller_json: *const c_char) {
    unsafe { logos_rust_sdk::set_call_caller(caller_json) }
}

extern "C" {
    fn lp_token_save_inbound(caller: *const c_char, token: *const c_char) -> c_int;
}

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn logos_module_accept_inbound_token(caller: *const c_char, token: *const c_char) -> c_int {
    if caller.is_null() || token.is_null() { return -1; }
    // INBOUND: `caller` is the module that will CALL US. This is not a
    // credential this module may present to anyone, and it must not
    // reach lp_token_save().
    unsafe { lp_token_save_inbound(caller, token) }
}
